newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended a lethargic day weak, with golds depressed by a weak bullion price and industrials easing in sympathy.
"We have seen negative sentiment creeping in from the bullion price," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.

The gold price was trading below $350 per ounce. Dealers said the bullion price looked vulnerable and if it did not pick up in the next few days, $340 per ounce would be the next target on the downside.
A lack of fresh factors saw industrials drifting lower. Dealers said a weak bond market also added to the negativity in the market.
They said the market also came off after the higher prices set during the March futures close-out on Monday and was trying to find a comfortable level and range.
Volumes were mediocre and dealers saw the market quiet ahead of the long weekend. Friday is a Human Rights Day holiday and next week sees the Easter long weekend.
The market on Wednesday would take its cue from Wall Street's performance, dealers said.
The overall index was off 26.9 points to 7,085.5, industrials lose 10.9 points to 8,321.6 and golds lose 20.4 points to 1,370.3.
De Beers was 75 cents weaker at 158.25 rand, Anglo shed 250 cents to 269.50 rand, Lonrho was down 10 cents to 10.20 rand and Stanbic gained 50 cents to 186.50 rand.
Among gold shares Dries ditched 75 cents to 43.25 rand, Kloof added 50 cents to 34.50 rand and Vaal Reefs clipped 500 cents to 292 rand.
Near-dated gold share futures ended soft on a weak bullion price and industrial contracts were hit by a softer bond market.
The June all-share contract was at 6,545/60 from 6,575, the industrial contract was at 8,170/73 from 8,198 and the gold contract was at 961/68 from 989.
